issue.title: replace tool turns literal Rust CRLF escapes into control characters
issue.body:
While editing a Rust HTTP test fixture with the built-in `replace` tool, `new_string` containing literal backslash-r/backslash-n sequences was written as control characters. The replacement reported success. Running rustfmt then left multiline strings with LF-only delimiters, and a local WebSocket handshake test timed out waiting for the HTTP header terminator.

The submitted replacement was Rust source `while !request.ends_with(b"\r\n\r\n") {` and an HTTP response string using the same escaped line endings. Reading the file after replacement and formatting showed a byte string containing two literal blank lines instead. A second replacement produced the same result. A unified diff applied with `apply_patch` preserved the Rust escape sequences, and the same test then passed.

Expected: exact text replacement preserves source-code escape sequences after JSON decoding, without an additional unescape pass.

Workload evidence: PR66 fixes in serdesAI, `serdes-ai-providers/examples/codex_haiku.rs`, macOS TS LLxprt driver using gpt-6-astra via codex. Local artifacts are `tmp/pr66-final-fixes/example-initial-handshake.log`, `example-line-ending-edit.log`, and passing `example.log`. No LLxprt implementation changes were made.

steps: Create http.rs with exactly this one-line Rust source and a final newline: fn main() { let x = b"old"; }. Read it with read_file.
expected: Exact replacement preserves literal source-code escape sequences after JSON decoding.
defect: replace writes physical newline/CR control characters where new_string contained literal backslash escape sequences, corrupting source code.
Root cause: The observed behavior is consistent with an additional escape-normalization step after JSON decoding, which makes literal backslash-n indistinguishable from an actual newline. The reports do not identify a confirmed implementation line; do not label an arbitrary edit helper as the root cause.
